Project: vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 7

**Boundary** — The behavioral trust surface. (1) `vinaya demo break`: create a deliberately malformed artifact on an isolated, discardable branch → commit-gate refusal with exact errors → guided fix → pass → cleanup instructions; rides the universal git-hook path so it works identically for every agent and human — the productized belief moment ("it actually stopped me"). (2) `vinaya waiver`: prompts for a short reason, then performs/instructs the forge-authenticated act — the principal-actor-applied `vinaya/waiver:docs` label per D-097 — that ring 1 honors; a waiver is NEVER an agent-emittable string (not body text, not a trailer, not a comment). NOT: the ring-1 actor-verification patch for THIS repo — aeg-governance-hardening task 29 (#380) ships and proves that mechanism first; this task productizes the proven pattern.

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (the demo story runs end-to-end on a fixture; a waiver label applied by a non-allowlisted actor is refused by the product's check; the human path works).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — vinaya.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: 4` (demo needs installed hooks; waiver needs config + labels present) and `aeg-governance-hardening #380` — the waiver mechanism must be proven live in this repo before Vinaya ships it to strangers (ratified sequencing, D-097).

**Traps to avoid** — Demo break must be truly isolated: never touches user branches, always cleans up, safe to run twice. The waiver command performs the forge act with the HUMAN's identity; in shared-credential setups (like this repo) the agent-session denial lives in the hook layer (mirror of task 29 part 2) — the one-line shared-credential caveat goes in the docs, per the TL's Q3 note. Ring-0 behavior on an unwaived violation is warn-with-declared-intent, never a hard block pre-PR (D-097 part 3).

**Suggested agent-class** — mid.

**Stop-and-escalate** — If the label-actor mechanism proves unimplementable for adopters on some GitHub plan/API tier, stop (`severity:strategy`).

**Docs to keep coherent** — `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` (trust-surface + waiver chapters, incl. the shared-credential caveat). Surfaces: `apps/vinaya/cli/**`.

Project: vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 6

**Boundary** — The installation-lifecycle triad: `vinaya doctor` (diagnoses hook presence/executability, workflow version vs config schema range, config validity, Node version, token scopes, branch-protection state report-only, custom-check registration + contract compliance, package skew; reports, NEVER mutates — D-089), `vinaya upgrade` (regenerates hooks/workflow/config with diff-and-confirm on any contract change; the only sanctioned migration path; compatible schema ranges, not exact pins — D-093), `vinaya eject` (removes every Vinaya artifact, returning the repo to stock in one command; reversibility is the trust prerequisite — D-089). NOT: demo/waiver (task 7); NOT shim state beyond a report placeholder.

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story — the full lifecycle on a fixture (init → doctor clean → perturb each diagnosable → doctor flags each → upgrade regenerates → eject → repo diff-identical to pre-init stock).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — vinaya.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: 4` — there is no installation to doctor/upgrade/eject before init exists.

**Traps to avoid** — Doctor NEVER mutates — every support interaction begins with its output; a doctor that "fixes" silently destroys that. Eject must remove EVERYTHING init installed — one surviving artifact breaks the reversibility claim; verify by diffing against pre-init stock. Version-skew failures self-explain ("run `vinaya upgrade`" — D-093); a bare mismatch error is a support ticket.

**Suggested agent-class** — mid.

**Stop-and-escalate** — If eject cannot cleanly restore stock for any artifact class, stop — a partial eject is worse than none.

**Docs to keep coherent** — `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` (lifecycle chapter). Surfaces: `apps/vinaya/cli/**`.

body:
Project: vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 4

**Boundary** — `npx vinaya init` + `vinaya init product`: the non-destructive-by-contract installer — detect git repo + `gh auth status`; print the COMPLETE diff of every intended change; require confirmation; then install: git pre-commit/pre-push hooks, `.github/workflows/vinaya.yml` (runs `vinaya check --all --diff-only`), `vinaya.config.json` seeded with the starter ruleset extracted from THIS repo's battle-tested gates (tier definitions, example doc-ownership bindings, brief-schema defaults, 2–3 real custom-check examples — D-105), issue/PR templates carrying the brief schema, labels (tiers + `vinaya/needs:execution-input`/`vinaya/needs:strategy-input`/`vinaya/needs:principal-input`), and the adopter decision-log scaffold (numbered entries: number, date, decision, rationale, locked gates affected — D-106); print (never apply) the recommended branch-protection command; `--dry-run` and `--yes` flags; final print names the next step (`vinaya demo break`). The interactive skeleton is harvested from Cetana's `apps/cetana-ai/cli/src/commands/init.ts` + its abort-path regression tests. `init product` scaffolds an additional governed product area in an initialized monorepo, same diff-and-confirm contract. NOT: doctor/upgrade/eject (task 6), demo/waiver (task 7); NOT running init on THIS repo (that is the migration iteration's move).

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (init on a clean fixture repo → every artifact present, workflow green, `--dry-run` output exactly matches what install then does, abort path exits clean), one agent holds it, bounded surface, single failure mode (installer wrote wrong/partial state — which the diff-and-confirm contract exists to prevent).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — vinaya.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: 3` — the workflow init installs invokes `vinaya check`; installing a workflow that calls a nonexistent command is not shippable.

**Traps to avoid** — NO postinstall — nothing executes on package install (D-084). NEVER touches PATH; NEVER writes branch protection (D-091) — print the command only. Abort paths: `process.stdin.destroy()` (Cetana PR #43's hang; port the regression test). Install-gate discipline (Cetana D-021/D-025, paid for twice): every code path Principal-runnable, not just the happy path. Starter-ruleset content is EXTRACTED from this repo's real gates, not invented defaults — blank-config paralysis is the failure it kills.

**Suggested agent-class** — high: wide surface, but every contract is fully specified.

**Stop-and-escalate** — Any mutation without a shown diff + explicit confirmation; any temptation toward postinstall or auto-applied branch protection → stop.

**Docs to keep coherent** — `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` (init contract + starter-ruleset chapters). Surfaces: `apps/vinaya/cli/**`.


---

**Amendment (2026-07-05, Planner) — HARD-STOP precondition added.** Do NOT brief this task until the governance-layout decision exists as a decision entry: whether `vinaya init` scaffolds governance data as a **data-only workspace package** (package.json + markdown, zero code) or as a bare root folder. Driver: `aeg-root/` sitting outside every workspace package defeats workspace-aware deploy-skip logic (confirmed live — docs-only plan PR #391 triggered 3 Vercel builds, 2 rate-limited); replicating that layout ships the cost to every adopter (finding `vinaya-finding-aeg-root-into-aeg-core`, Principal-directed HIGH). Planner recommendation on record: sibling data package, NOT folded into aeg-core (engine ships via npm; governance data is repo-local content the engine reads). Brief Author: if no such decision entry exists at dig time, stop and escalate `severity:strategy`. Related: D-085's "zero gain" clause is flagged for reconciliation at the ratification window (PR #415). The extraction source list for the starter ruleset is in this Issue's comments (2026-07-05 audit).


**Amendment (2026-07-05, Planner) — hook-installation semantics made explicit** (routed finding: `vinaya-finding-husky-hook-installation`). No new decision entry needed — all three points derive from D-089 (non-destructive trust surface) + this task's own diff-and-confirm contract: (1) installed git hooks are thin, clearly-delimited STUBS that invoke the installed `vinaya` binary (`vinaya check`-family) — never inlined check logic, and never paths into this monorepo's `packages/aeg-core/bin/*` (that is this repo's shim wiring, not the product's); this matches the thin-dispatcher shape `.husky/pre-push` here has been converging to (tasks 25/32/33). (2) Pre-existing adopter hooks are NEVER clobbered: if a hook file exists, vinaya appends a delimited managed block (marker comments), shown verbatim in the diff-and-confirm output before anything is written; if none exists, it generates the stub fresh; `vinaya eject` removes exactly the managed block, or the whole file only if vinaya created it. (3) Hook-manager strategy — husky detected vs raw `.git/hooks`/`core.hooksPath` — is a Brief-Author dig-time call; if no clean activation path exists for a target repo shape, stop-and-escalate `severity:strategy` rather than inventing a new hook manager. Per-clone hook-presence drift is `vinaya doctor`'s job (#386), not the installer's — installer installs, doctor diagnoses.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — workflow-installation semantics made explicit** (routed finding: `vinaya-finding-workflow-naming-convention`). Same shape as the hook amendment; no new decision entry needed — the naming rule already exists in D-085 ("machine-generated artifacts in adopter repos carry a `vinaya-` prefix") and the single-workflow design in D-104/the §5 contract. Explicit now: (1) init installs exactly ONE workflow file, `.github/workflows/vinaya.yml` (running `vinaya check --all --diff-only`) — enforcement consolidates behind the check engine, so there is no generated workflow *family*; if a future task ever generates additional workflows, D-085's `vinaya-` prefix is the mandatory scheme. (2) GitHub Actions reads workflow files ONLY flat inside `.github/workflows/` (no subfolder scanning) — no design here depends on subfolders, so this is recorded as a constraint, not a risk; the Developer may confirm it empirically in one line if any doubt arises during implementation. (3) Never-clobber applies to workflows exactly as to hooks: if `.github/workflows/vinaya.yml` already exists with content vinaya did not generate, init REFUSES to overwrite (shown in the diff-and-confirm output; explicit `--force`-class confirmation or manual resolution required); `vinaya eject` removes the file only if vinaya owns it. (4) Tier distinction recorded: `.github/workflows/` + `.husky/` are the MANDATORY enforcement substrate the installer must handle correctly; `.claude/**` (or any other assistant-specific projection) is OUT of this task's scope entirely — optional, tool-specific, never a blocker for Vinaya's core function (consistent with D-072's black-box principle). (5) This repo's own un-prefixed AEG workflows (`archivist.yml`, `forge-lifecycle.yml`, `verify-docs.yml`, `verify-test-plan.yml`) are REPLACED by the generated file at the `aeg-forge-state-v1` cutover, not renamed — no separate rename task exists; `ci.yml`/`conventions.yml`/`claude*.yml` are monorepo-generic and keep their names.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — full install manifest, consolidated.** Fills the remaining gaps the prior three amendments left implicit. This table is the §4 surface-map starting point; it does not repeat the hook/workflow amendments' prose, only what wasn't yet explicit:

| Artifact | Filename freedom? | Naming | Collision rule | Eject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CI workflow | free (flat dir) | `vinaya.yml`, future extras `vinaya-*` (D-085) | refuse if foreign content exists at that path | delete |
| Git hooks | fixed names | n/a | marker-delimited managed block, never clobber | remove block, or file if vinaya-created |
| **Issue template** | free (dir holds many) | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/vinaya-task.md` | new file only; never touches adopter templates | delete |
| **PR template** | fixed name (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) | n/a | same managed-block/refuse-if-foreign rule as hooks — GitHub allows only one, never clobber | remove block/file per ownership |
| Config (D-105 starter ruleset) | free | `vinaya.config.json` | diff-and-confirm if exists | delete |
| **Labels** (tiers, `needs:*-input`) | n/a — forge objects | AEG vocabulary as-is | create if absent; **existing labels are never modified** | documented removal, listed by eject, not auto-deleted (labels may be in use elsewhere) |
| Branch protection | n/a | n/a | never installed — command printed only (D-091, already in Traps above) | n/a |
| **Adopter decision-log scaffold** (D-106) | free | rides the governance-layout decision | new files | delete |
| `.claude/**` or other assistant-specific projection | n/a | n/a | **not installed at all** — out of v1.0 scope (workflow amendment point 4) | n/a |

Two rows (`decision-log scaffold` location, and by extension where any other governance-data seed lands) remain gated on the governance-layout decision named in the hard-stop amendment above — that decision is not yet made; this table does not resolve it, only inventories what depends on it.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — hard-stop precondition status: entry now exists, ratification still owed.** D-110 (governance-state disposition) and D-111 (protocol/doctrine distribution) are logged in `aeg-project/decisions.md`, both `Status: PENDING`, queued at `ratification-queue.md` alongside D-083–109. This satisfies the amendment-2 hard-stop's literal precondition ("the governance-layout decision exists as a decision entry") — the Brief Author is no longer blind on this task's design. It does NOT yet satisfy dispatchability: a brief executing a PENDING Type 1 decision is not dispatchable (standing rule, same as every other D-083–109-dependent brief this iteration) — do not author or dispatch this task's brief until D-110/D-111 are ratified. See D-110/D-111 directly for the resolved shape (state disposition table, package-wrapped file residue, doctrine bundled-in-package + scaffolded pointer) — amendment 4's install manifest table above remains accurate and unchanged by this resolution.

body:
Project: vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 3

**Boundary** — The check engine: `vinaya check <name> | --all` with `--json` (versioned envelope), `--diff-only` (change-surface scope; the ring-1 default), `--parallel` (concurrency-capped); the error-output contract on ALL checks — structured JSON lines on stderr, exit 0/1, per-check timeout enforced by the RUNNER, no-network-by-default, every error carrying `agent_recovery_prompt` (D-100); the core AEG gates (doc coverage, brief shape, coherence, dispatch readiness) expressed through the SAME interface as custom checks — no privileged API (D-092/D-104); custom-check registration via `vinaya.config.json` (any executable honoring the contract; glob scoping allowed, conditionals forbidden — D-109); and `vinaya new check` scaffolding from a worked template. NOT: the CI workflow install (task 4's `vinaya.yml`); NOT edits to `packages/aeg-core/bin/*`; NOT the shim.

**Sizing** — Passes, at the top of the size range: one verification story (a fixture repo's checks all run through one interface — core and custom indistinguishable to the runner; contract violations surfaced by contract tests), bounded surface, one failure-mode family (runner/contract). If the Brief Author's dig shows the runner and the core-gate expression are separately verifiable, escalate a split rather than silently absorbing it.

**Project(s) + blast radius** — vinaya. Consumes `@atta/aeg-core` + `apps/vinaya/sources` read-only through their public exports; needs no edits there — task 2 delivered the seams. Needing a core edit is a stop condition, not scope creep.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: 1` (bin/config/envelope), `2` (StateSource — checks read state ONLY through it; "no check binary hardcodes a state path" is the ratified corollary).

**Traps to avoid** — `agent_recovery_prompt` is the corrective INSTRUCTION ("You modified X but not its owning doc Y. Read Y, apply your change, commit both."), never the diagnosis restated. Timeouts live in the runner, not in checks. The error schema is a versioned public surface (D-100/D-103) — additive evolution only. Do not let core checks grow a private fast path — no-privileged-API is the product's extensibility claim.

**Suggested agent-class** — high: contract design + runner semantics.

**Stop-and-escalate** — Any core gate that cannot be expressed through the public check interface without privilege → stop (`severity:strategy`; that is a contract gap). Any need to edit aeg-core → stop.

**Docs to keep coherent** — `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` (check contract + error schema chapters — the doc plugins are written against). Surfaces: `apps/vinaya/cli/**`.

body:
Project: aeg-core, vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 2

**Boundary** — The StateSource seam, split per aeg-core's purity charter: (a) in `@atta/aeg-core` src: the StateSource CONTRACT only — types plus any derivation-seam adjustments so the pure evaluators consume state through the contract (aeg-core stays zero-I/O, post-#372 shape); (b) in a NEW third vinaya workspace, `apps/vinaya/sources`: BOTH implementations — forge-backed (the primary design; copy-adapt Studio's `apps/aeg/web/studio/src/lib/forge/*` fetchers; Studio's own copy untouched) and file-backed (transitional; wraps the existing `parseIteration`/`parseLedger`/`parseRegistry` readers over `aeg-root/`), selected by config. NOT: rewiring `packages/aeg-core/bin/*` gates onto StateSource — that cutover is `aeg-forge-state-v1`'s entire job (the birth rule: gates read files until the migration flips the config in one deliberate act); NOT Studio changes (vinaya-studio-v1 task 2).

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (both adapters produce IDENTICAL derived state for this repo — golden forge-vs-file comparison), one agent holds it, bounded surface (aeg-core types + one new package), single failure mode (adapter divergence).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — aeg-core, vinaya. The aeg-core change is additive types — consumers (Studio, gates, CI) need re-verification (compile + existing tests) only, no edits. `apps/vinaya/sources` is new code.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: aeg-governance-hardening #372` (task 28 purifies aeg-core to gray-matter-only; building the contract before that lands means building on a package being reshaped the same week). `Conflicts-with: aeg-governance-hardening 25` (same aeg-core collision domain while 25 is in flight). Mechanically gated regardless: `Project: aeg-core` is undispatchable until aeg-governance-hardening fully archives (verify-dispatch's prior-iteration predicate).

**Traps to avoid** — Adapters NEVER land in aeg-core — no octokit/gh/network dependency enters the package (#372's purity is the charter; violating it re-pollutes the package the week it was purified). Forge-backed is the PRIMARY design — every external adopter is forge-native from day one; file-backed is the deliberate THROWAWAY (deleted by the migration iteration) — invert any instinct to polish the file side. `verify-coherence.ts` has its own forge-fetch path — leave it untouched. Un-targeted `gh` calls from linked worktrees resolve the wrong repo (fixed pattern in #374 — reuse it). Publish-time packaging of `sources` relative to the "CLI surgically small" rule (D-084/D-104) is a LAUNCH-iteration question — record it in the package README so it isn't rediscovered; do not solve it here (Principal directive, 2026-07-04).

**Suggested agent-class** — high: the architectural keystone; the contract shape outlives everything else in the iteration.

**Stop-and-escalate** — If the contract cannot stay pure in aeg-core without an I/O dependency, stop (`severity:strategy`). If the forge and file adapters cannot produce identical derived state for this repo, stop — the divergence is a design finding, never something to paper over.

**Docs to keep coherent** — Surfaces: `packages/aeg-core/src/**`, `apps/vinaya/sources/**`. Docs: `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` (StateSource chapter), `docs-index.md` (new files), and the `sources` package README (packaging note above). doc-owners derivation at brief time is the floor.


---

**Amendment (2026-07-05, Planner) — requirement added to Boundary/Traps.** The file-backed StateSource implementation MUST take its governance root as a configuration parameter (defaulting to `aeg-root/`), never a hardcoded path constant spread through read sites. Driver: the governance-layout finding (`vinaya-finding-aeg-root-into-aeg-core`, 2026-07-05, Principal-directed) may relocate this repo's governance data into a data-only workspace package; with a config-parameterized root that relocation is a config flip, without it a rewrite. The forge-backed source is unaffected. Decision pending in Strategist mode — see the hard-stop amendment on #384.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — concrete forge-object mapping (supersedes the generic "forge-backed" placeholder); real-data validation added to Sizing.** Per D-110 (PENDING — cite it, do not re-derive): the forge-backed adapter's concrete shape is now decided, not open. Map: iteration Goal/Lifecycle → **Milestone** (one per iteration); task→iteration membership → the EXISTING `vinaya/iteration:<slug>` label + Issue rationale (no new mechanism — already forge-native today); token reports → **Issue/PR comments**, summed at read time; lessons + per-project operational state → **one pinned Issue each**. Do NOT build a Discussions or Projects-v2 client — D-110 deliberately excludes both (minimal-surface-area requirement for a light product); the forge-backed adapter's dependency footprint is Issues + Labels + Comments + Milestones only, nothing else.

**Sizing addendum — validate against THIS repo's real data, not a fixture.** The golden forge-vs-file comparison (Sizing, above) must run against real, already-existing iteration data in this repo (e.g. `vinaya-cli-v1` or `vinaya-studio-v1`'s own topology), not synthetic fixtures alone — prove the mechanism against real complexity before the rest of the CLI (tasks 3–7) builds on top of it. This mirrors the repo's own canonized lesson from Cetana's Slice-1 prototype (`cetana-experiment-log.md` §6: "validate the existential dependency before building the product") — the same discipline applied to StateSource. If a cheap, pre-task validation is wanted even before this task is briefed, a throwaway, ungoverned spike (outside the AEG task/Issue machinery entirely, same as Cetana's own prototype at `~/code/cetana-prototype/`) is the Principal's option, not a requirement of this task.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — spike evidence: real finding on Depends-on parsing.** A pre-task validation spike (outside the AEG task machinery, no dispatch — mirrors Cetana's Slice-1 precedent) proved the two D-110 mechanisms nothing has tested yet: a scratch Milestone round-tripped Goal text + open/closed↔active/complete Lifecycle exactly; a scratch Issue's comment thread round-tripped an ordered log exactly (both objects deleted/closed after). It ALSO surfaced a real gap: this Issue's own `Dependency rationale` field writes its second edge (`2`) as separate prose with its own backtick span, not the topology file's single `1, 2` value — a naive line-based parser silently drops it. **Requirement added:** the forge-backed adapter's Depends-on/Conflicts-with extraction must tolerate multiple backtick-quoted numeric tokens per field (not assume one comma-joined value), OR the D-078 rationale grammar must be tightened to require exactly one comma-joined value per field — Brief Author's dig should pick one and state which; do not silently assume the clean case.


**Amendment (2026-07-06, Planner) — resequencing (D-112): scope shrinks from "build" to "consume."** `aeg-forge-state-v1` (D-112) now runs BEFORE this iteration and builds the generic forge-reading adapter itself (task 1, #425) as its own package, proven against this repo's real, live governance data — not a fixture. `Depends-on` now includes `aeg-forge-state-v1 #425` alongside the existing `aeg-governance-hardening #372`. **This task's Boundary changes accordingly:** the forge-backed half of the StateSource seam is no longer built here from scratch — it is IMPORTED or RE-HOMED from `aeg-forge-state-v1`'s already-working, already-battle-tested package into `apps/vinaya/sources`. Remaining scope: the pure CONTRACT in `@atta/aeg-core` (unchanged), the file-backed transitional adapter (unchanged, still built here), and wiring the imported/re-homed forge adapter behind the same contract. The golden forge-vs-file comparison (Sizing) is correspondingly cheaper — the forge side already has a proven track record from #425, not a fresh implementation needing its own from-scratch validation. Brief Author: confirm at dig time whether `aeg-forge-state-v1`'s package is imported as a dependency or physically re-homed into `apps/vinaya/sources` — either is acceptable; state which and why.

body:
Project: vinaya
Iteration: vinaya-cli-v1 · task 1

**Boundary** — Create the `apps/vinaya/cli` workspace package: `vinaya` bin entry + command router (help/version skeleton only), hierarchical config loader (repo-local `vinaya.config.json` over `~/.vinaya/config.json`) harvested from Cetana's `apps/cetana-ai/cli/src/lib/config.ts` + its precedence regression tests (copy-adapt; Cetana itself untouched — deletion is a later, deferred iteration), and the versioned `--json` output envelope (a `schema` version field on all machine output from day one — D-100/D-103). Seed `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-spec.md` + `apps/vinaya/specs/vinaya-backlog.md` from the ratified D-083+ set, plus `apps/vinaya/CLAUDE.md`/README. NOT: any real command logic (checks, init, forge writes — later tasks); NO `@atta/aeg-core` import yet (keeps this task pure-`Project: vinaya` and mechanically dispatchable ahead of the gov-hardening archive, if the Principal chooses); no npm publish shape.

**Sizing** — Passes the four tests: one verification story (bin runs; config precedence tests green; envelope versioned), one agent holds it, bounded new-package surface (harvest is ~555 lines incl. tests), single failure mode.

**Project(s) + blast radius** — vinaya only. The new workspace is matched by the existing `apps/*/*` glob; root lockfile churn is expected and not a collision (re-verify no other open task edits it at dispatch).

**Dependency rationale** — None. First dispatchable task of the iteration by construction.

**Traps to avoid** — Cetana's install-gate lessons are already paid for — port them, don't relearn them: `bun link` is not a workspace script (`cd apps/vinaya/cli && bun link`); interactive abort paths must destroy stdin (Cetana PR #43's hang).
